drawdown_context: Indiana-based diversified bank holding company ($18.8B assets) focused on multi-family/healthcare agency mortgage banking, mortgage warehouse lending to non-depository mortgage bankers, and traditional Indiana community banking. FY24 10-K reports record net income of $320.4M (+15% YoY), EPS $6.30 (+12%), tangible book value $34.15 (+25%), CET1 ratio comfortably above well-capitalized minimums, and 7th consecutive year of growth — yet underneath, NPLs more than tripled ($82.0M -> $279.7M / 0.80% -> 2.68% of loans), Substandard loans more than doubled ($128.6M -> $317.3M), Special Mention loans doubled ($191M -> $380M), ACL coverage of NPLs collapsed from 87% to 30%, FHLB advances exploded 441% from $771M to $4.17B, and the company laid on $2.9B of credit-protection synthetic risk transfers (CDS / credit-linked notes) to keep risk-weighted assets down. Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-09, 6 days pre-cutoff): EPS halved ($1.80 -> $0.93, -48%), NIM compressed 25bps to 2.89%, efficiency ratio jumped 13 percentage points, provision +63%, and tangible book value still growing — narrative of solvent growth despite multi-family credit stress consistent with control_survivor classification, but credit deterioration trajectory and balance-sheet engineering are real signals worth scoring.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K audit report: Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm (Forvis Mazars, LLP, Indianapolis, Indiana, PCAOB ID 686). 'We have served as the Company's auditor since 2014.' Unqualified opinion. Critical Audit Matter: 'Allowance for Credit Losses on Multi-family Financing Loans Collectively Evaluated - Refer to Notes 1 and 5... determining the qualitative reserve estimate required significant judgment.' No going-concern paragraph; no substantial-doubt language anywhere in 10-K.
rfm_tuples.f: going_concern_local on 10-K AND on pre-cutoff Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-09); auditor_change_tracker; Mode B: did the next periodic filing escalate disclosure? Does the CAM align with the area that actually deteriorated?
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K: signal=NO_GOING_CONCERN, n_matches=0 ('going concern' / 'substantial doubt' / 'cease operations'). Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-09): also NO_GOING_CONCERN. Auditor Forvis Mazars (rebranded BKD; merged with Mazars 2024) since 2014, 11-year tenure, no resignation/disagreement language. CAM is precisely the multi-family ACL — the very area where NPLs tripled.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is technically clean and auditor stayed. But the auditor's sole CAM is the qualitative ACL on multi-family financing — exactly the area where Substandard loans grew 147%, NPLs grew 241%, and ACL-coverage-of-NPL collapsed from 87% to 30%. The CAM is a pre-warning that the auditor itself flagged the reserves as judgmentally fragile. Auditor brand-step-down note: Forvis Mazars is regional (rebranded BKD), not Big 4 — consistent with company history but represents a lower disclosure-stress signal than peers with Big 4 auditors.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Credit-quality cliff metrics (FY23 -> FY24): NPL UPB $82.0M -> $279.7M (+241%); NPL % of loans 0.80% -> 2.68% (+235bp); Special Mention $191.3M -> $380.0M (+99%); Substandard $128.6M -> $317.3M (+147%); ACL coverage of NPLs 87% -> 30%. Q1 2025 10-Q: NPLs $284.6M (+2% QoQ, still bumping); Substandard $323.6M (+2% QoQ); Special Mention $407.9M (+7% QoQ); ACL coverage of NPLs 29% (essentially unchanged, still half of FY23's level). Mode B is the verification gap: management's 'asset values remain strong overall' framing is contradicted by the ACL/NPL ratio mechanics — if collateral were genuinely strong, the ACL would not need to be only 30% of NPLs (51%+ is industry-typical for multifamily distress). The 'expected improvement with rate cuts' thesis was already half-falsified by Q1 2025 — NPLs and adversely classified loans continued ticking up despite the late-2024 rate cuts and into Q1 2025. Continuing credit deterioration with thin reserves is the textbook 'extend-and-hope' setup.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note 14: Total borrowings: FHLB advances $4,172,030 thousand (Dec 2024) vs $771,392 thousand (Dec 2023), +441%. 'The increase was primarily due to $3.4 billion in additional FHLB advances. The higher level of collateralized borrowing was primarily due to it being a more cost-effective funding option than utilizing brokered deposits.' Brokered deposits dropped $5.97B -> $2.53B (-58%).
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on funding-mix evolution; Mode B: is the 'cost-effective' framing the real reason for the FHLB spike, or is brokered-deposit reliance being swapped for FHLB reliance to make the deposit table look better? Cross-check uninsured deposit %.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Funding mix shift FY23 -> FY24: Brokered deposits down $3.4B (-58%); FHLB advances up $3.4B (+441%). Net wholesale funding (brokered + FHLB): $6.74B (FY23) -> $6.71B (FY24) — essentially UNCHANGED. The 'core deposits 79% vs 58%' improvement is mostly a re-classification: core deposits grew $1.3B but the brokered drop was 2.5x larger. Q1 2025 10-Q: FHLB advances $3.85B (down from $4.17B), brokered $1.72B (down from $2.53B), core deposits $10.69B (+14% QoQ). Uninsured deposits ~24% of total ($2.8B) — moderate. 'Our line of credit with the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, alone, could fund 111% of uninsured deposits.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A: numbers reconcile. Mode B: the deposit-mix improvement story conceals that NET wholesale funding (brokered + FHLB) was essentially unchanged at ~$6.7B. The 'cost-effective' framing is plausible (FHLB at 2.78-4.48% vs brokered CD rates 5%+), but the optical narrative of 'core deposits 79%' obscures continued ~36% reliance on wholesale funding. Real positive: uninsured deposit ratio (24%) is moderate and Fed discount window backstop is sized to cover. Dressed-up but not deceptive. Note: warehouse-customer custodial deposits are technically core but functionally wholesale — concentration risk flagged in own risk factors.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'In April of 2023, as well as March and December of 2024, the Company strategically executed credit protection arrangements through a credit linked note and credit default swaps, totaling $2.9 billion in loans on the closing date, to reduce risk of losses, with incremental coverage ranging from 13-14% of the unpaid principal balances for each arrangement. As of December 31, 2024, the balance of loans in credit protection arrangements was $2.3 billion, compared to $934.6 million as of December 31, 2023.' Credit linked notes carried at $84.4M (Dec 2024) vs $119.9M (Dec 2023).
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on synthetic risk transfer; Mode B: what is the function of these structures — bona fide hedging, regulatory capital arbitrage, or a way to keep RWA down while NPL deterioration accelerates?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Stack of synthetic risk transfers: April 2023 (credit-linked note), March 2024 ($543.5M CDS on multifamily pool), December 2024 ($1.2B CDS on warehouse loans). Total $2.9B closing notional; $2.3B outstanding at Dec 2024. 13-14% credit protection. Effect: lowers risk-weighted assets, but the bank retains first-loss + most upside via insurance accounting. 13-14% protection is meaningful but small relative to worst-case loss in a multi-family credit cycle. CDS counterparty is undisclosed in the 10-K narrative.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A: structures are disclosed. Mode B: $2.9B notional of synthetic risk transfers in 21 months — including the December 2024 $1.2B WAREHOUSE CDS — is unusual for a bank claiming 'strong asset values' and 'lower than industry charge-offs.' Either (a) management genuinely sees brewing losses they're hedging, or (b) regulatory capital optimization to support a 10x leverage business while reported NPL coverage thins. Either reading is informative. The December 2024 CDS is on WAREHOUSE loans (mortgage banker funding facilities) — not the deteriorating multi-family book — suggesting management is preparing for a stressed-warehouse-customer scenario they're not narrating. The synthetic risk transfer activity is the most informative Mode B tell about management's true credit view.

Q1 2025 10-Q: warehouse loans funded $11.9B in Q1 alone (+49% YoY), accelerating, but the December 2024 $1.2B warehouse-CDS protection is a concrete signal that management was concerned. Mode B verification gap: no named counterparty disclosure (peers like FBC, EFSC typically disclose top-5 warehouse client share); no quantitative concentration metric ('significant portion' is undefined). The credit-default-swap on warehouse loans in December 2024 is the implied verification.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A: existence-check passes (concentration is acknowledged). Mode B: verification is asymmetric — company describes the risk qualitatively but withholds quantitative disclosure (no top-N customer share, no counterparty names, no specific deposit-concentration ratio). The December 2024 $1.2B WAREHOUSE CDS purchase is the deterministic flag that management's internal view of warehouse-counterparty stress is more elevated than the narrative suggests. In a regional-bank context where 2023 saw multiple bank failures triggered by concentrated non-depository deposit relationships, MBIN's combination of (a) growing warehouse origination 38% YoY, (b) refusing to name top customers, and (c) simultaneously buying $1.2B of warehouse CDS — is the implied-verification pattern of a bank not lying but very quietly building defenses.

summary: Merchants Bancorp is a profitable, well-capitalized Indiana regional bank holding company whose FY24 10-K is TECHNICALLY HONEST about a meaningful but contained multi-family/healthcare credit cycle. Mode A verification: most claims reconcile to the data (no fraud, no auditor change, no going-concern language, dividend coverage genuinely strong, capital ratios solidly above well-capitalized). Mode B (the discriminating signals): (1) NPLs +241% YoY with ACL coverage collapsed from 87% to 30%, continuing flat-to-up in Q1 2025; (2) modifications up 30x YoY with 22% re-default rate — classical extend-and-pretend pattern; (3) $2.9B notional of synthetic risk transfers in 21 months, including a Dec 2024 $1.2B WAREHOUSE CDS (counterparty-distress hedge that contradicts narrative silence on warehouse customer names); (4) CEO Petrie made a 975,610-share family-trust gift on Dec 11 2024 at near-peak price (~$40), with zero insider open-market buys in the Feb 28 - May 9 window despite continued credit deterioration; (5) deposit-mix 'improvement' (core deposits 58% -> 79%) is mostly re-classification — net wholesale funding (brokered + FHLB) essentially unchanged at $6.7B FY24 vs FY23; (6) warehouse origination +38% YoY (vs +9% industry) implies counterparty-quality drift, consistent with the simultaneous warehouse-CDS hedging; (7) auditor (Forvis Mazars, rebranded BKD) is regional not Big 4, and the lone CAM is precisely the multi-family ACL that subsequently degraded. Framework verdict: this is a CONTROL_SURVIVOR-tier name correctly — the equity is supported by strong franchise economics, founding-family alignment (57% stake), capital flexibility, and sustainable dividend; but the credit-cycle stress is real and the implied-verification signals (modifications, CDS hedges, insider absence-of-buying, modification re-defaults, ACL thinness) suggest the framework should classify as NEUTRAL-with-credit-risk-overlay rather than clean LONG. Honesty-alpha framing: management is honest at the data level and obscuring only at the narrative-framing level — the framework can catch this with Mode B claim-evolution checks but should not overweight to SHORT because the dividend/capital/auditor/insider-stake fundamentals are real.
